body.text: Reconstruction v1 recorded as r0005 (output contract VALID, quality FAIL). Its 3D opposition fractions .246 white/.096 black expose a weakness of closest-any-probe contact fitting, and FCL finds finger self-intersection in .478 of valid frames. I copied the required MANO fitter to research/handlib_opposed (installed copy untouched), adding losses for thumb/index regional surface contact and separation in the visually observed hold intervals (white f98–175, black f283–365), plus distal finger centreline separation. This is inferred contact supervision, not measured force/contact ground truth. Config increases penetration weight .05 to .3, depth-order 0 to .15, frees scale prior 1 to .3 and runs 800 iterations. Will compare image IoU, opposed contacts and self-intersections before keeping it.

Constrained reference estimates (preliminary): white f100–140 rotates 71.6deg relative to MANO wrist while wrist rotates 31.6deg. Black f310–340 initially appears 174.6deg because a 180deg identical-blade yaw branch was inconsistent; the equivalent continuous branch is 65.2deg about approximately object +x. Testing the equivalent final black yaw branch before relying on its interval. MoGe table normal predicts about 17mm inconsistent initial support heights for the known-side-resting objects; shared planar support plus visible vertical blade direction suggests a 12deg camera pitch correction (down normal approx [.016,.815,.579] rather than [.016,.665,.747]). Re-fitting both objects with this physical prior, retaining silhouette comparison and uncertainty. This normal is an estimate using physical relations, not an independent calibration.

FCL pair diagnosis of the contact-aware fit: middle/ring intersect in 105 supported frames, including black turn f283–294 and f307 onward; thumb/index in 4 approach/withdrawal frames, index/middle in 3 white-turn frames f139–141. The first separation loss omitted MCP-to-PIP shafts even though the checked distal MANO skin regions include part of them. Extending the centreline loss to the MCP and using 16mm separation (about twice a finger half-width) is a targeted fit correction. Rounded housing collision meshes now match the reconstruction surfaces rather than conservative boxes. Will re-score and inspect imagery.

Scene refinement result: freeing yaw while constraining observed blade direction raised median white care-IoU to .894. Joint stationary-object camera/plane fit then gives .884 white/.825 black, about .010/.031 lower than before, in exchange for physically stationary supports. Fitted gravity down in camera0 [.0884,.7186,.6898], support-height residuals <0.7mm, estimated camera translation up to 39.5mm. These quantities depend on assumed metric housing dimensions and are not independently calibrated. The earlier trial with an imposed normal lost ~.15 IoU and was rejected; the joint fitted normal resolves that tradeoff.

The explicit blade-pair correction raises white tracker median care-IoU to .901 and removes the x/y silhouette ambiguity. Its coherent camera/support re-fit changes inferred normal and object depths; the warm-start MANO fit has lower median silhouette IoU (.777 versus .847 on the prior ambiguous scene), despite retaining contact. Testing a final image-weight refinement (silhouette100->200, depth-order.15->.05, physical contact/separation unchanged) to recover image agreement without reintroducing penetration. All parameters and uncertainty are retained; no simulation or training yet.

Correctly re-expressing the earlier clean MANO fit into the updated camera frame recovers median mask IoU .8449 with sampled max penetration .8mm and .401mm jitter. The previous warm start had mixed world coordinates across calibrations, causing a regression; it is rejected. The recovered fit fixes shape at the earlier well-supported betas, refits pose/depth/scale against the blade-corrected scene, and retains the same validity rule. Running full validation before recording it. Remaining reconstruction time is reserved for checks, uncertainty, criteria and records, not robot simulation.

This supports a thumb/opposing-index rolling skill with occasional middle support. Reconstruction is frozen; proceed to physical robot simulation and primitive feasibility.

Failure montage shows index contact at blade base causes4.6mm metal/fingertip intersection, then the plug falls within.15s; some starts exceed joint speed limits. Larger Wuji pads cannot copy the human index-on-blade patch exactly. I am moving index contact to the housing lateral pad below the blades, retaining opposed thumb/index rolling, and adding full collision residuals to IK. Also modelling nested two-axis MCP/CMC palm housings as adjacent internal geometry: their provided convex CAD parts overlap in zero pose, so only palm-vs-first-two-joint housing pairs are excluded; all exterior finger-finger/object collisions remain active. Testing a thumb-normal-only IK constraint instead of a full thumb twist, retaining index pad rotation and physical collisions, to give the coupled fingertip path more workspace. Wrist assist target14deg remains below the recorded15deg bound; fingers must still do most of the turn.

Kinematic diagnosis from the recorded reconstruction: the white pre-turn wrist/object configuration requires index extension for blades-up (root rotation axis mostly-X), and my tested paths hit the indexPIP stop and drop. The clearer black pre-turn reference has blade axis mostly wrist-Y and requires positive-X finger closing; its wrist is more upright, exactly as the demonstrator holds it.
